short: Reunified China after three centuries of division, then destroyed itself in a generation.
full:
Yang Jian, a general of mixed Chinese and Xianbei descent serving the Northern Zhou, took the throne from his infant grandson in 581 and ruled as Emperor Wen. In 589 his armies crossed the Yangtze and extinguished the Chen, ending the division that had lasted since 420. He rebuilt the capital at Daxing, later Chang'an, restored the equal-field system that allotted land to peasant households, codified the law, and began recruiting officials by written examination rather than birth alone.

His son Yang Guang, Emperor Yang, inherited a solvent state and spent it. He completed the Grand Canal linking the Yangtze rice lands to the northern frontier, rebuilt Luoyang as a second capital, and between 612 and 614 launched three invasions of Goguryeo in Korea, each of which failed with heavy losses. Conscription and taxation on that scale broke the countryside; rebellions spread from Shandong outward, and in 618 the emperor was strangled by his own guards at Jiangdu. His cousin Li Yuan founded the Tang, which kept nearly every Sui institution.
